rationale: This is literally the intersection of two archived winners (WeakestLinkQualityProfit and AbnormalCycleWeakestLink) that share the identical profitability leg, and the archive already showed that adding a third hurdle to the two-hurdle conjunction degrades rather than improves both fmb_tstat and alpha, so it is a cosmetic leg-substitution with little independent information.

Applying the weakest-link operator across time rather than across dimensions is a structurally new construct that is internally consistent (a high three-year minimum of a bounded joint percentile genuinely means "never failed"), with the only caveats being the added history requirement on coverage and its high correlation with the archived single-year conjunction.

The diagnosis of the archived consistency signal is technically correct — multiplying a positive profitability rank by a signed industry z-score inverts the ordering in the negative tail — and recasting sign-frequency as a bounded hurdle is the right repair, though the 0–5 count is coarse and will generate heavy ties inside the MIN.

Both leg upgrades were independently validated in the archive, the expression matches the stated hypothesis with the correct natural sign, and the explicit avoidance of double-counting the same single-year accrual in numerator and hurdle shows the construct was thought through rather than assembled mechanically.

Embedding the cash-build channel as a bounded rank hurdle is a sensible repair and brings a non-working-capital validation channel into the conjunctive family, but the stated diagnosis is somewhat wrong (the archived version was already winsorized and z-scored, so the failure was the signed-multiplier inversion, not unboundedness) and cumulative cash accumulation risks proxying for known cash-holdings/issuance effects.

Decomposing the winning profit-per-accrual-capital ratio into margin and working-capital velocity is a legitimate diagnostic question and the accrual leg is a new combination rather than a rediscovery, but each individual component (gross margin, turnover, working-capital accruals) is a well-known published anomaly and the triple-MIN structure risks the same redundancy that weakened the archived triple hurdle.
